questions.q: What is the first-order necessary condition for x* to be an unconstrained local minimum of a differentiable f?
options: The Hessian at x* is negative definite
The gradient ∇f(x*) equals zero
x* must be a global maximum of -f
questions.explain: At a smooth local minimum there is no direction that decreases f further, which requires every partial derivative — the gradient — to vanish.

questions.q: A critical point has a Hessian with one positive and one negative eigenvalue. What kind of point is it?
options: A strict local minimum
A strict local maximum
A saddle point
It cannot be a critical point
questions.explain: Mixed-sign Hessian eigenvalues mean the function curves up in one direction and down in another — the signature of a saddle point, not a minimum or maximum.

questions.q: For f(x) = ½xᵀAx − bᵀx with A symmetric positive definite, what is the closed-form minimizer?
options: x* = Ab
x* = A⁻¹b
x* = b⁻¹A
x* = 2Ab
questions.explain: Setting the gradient Ax − b to zero gives Ax = b, so x* = A⁻¹b.

questions.q: Why does Newton's method reach the exact minimum of a purely quadratic function in a single step?
options: Because the step size is always chosen to equal 1
Because the function's curvature (its Hessian) is constant everywhere, so the local quadratic model is exact
Because Newton's method ignores the gradient entirely
Because quadratic functions have no local minima
questions.explain: Newton's method fits a local quadratic approximation and jumps to its minimum. When f is itself exactly quadratic, that local model is the function everywhere, so one step lands exactly on x*.

questions.q: What is the main practical trade-off between gradient descent and Newton's method?
options: Gradient descent needs many cheap steps; Newton's method needs fewer but costlier steps requiring the Hessian
Gradient descent only works on convex functions while Newton's method works on any function
Newton's method never requires computing derivatives
There is no meaningful trade-off; Newton's method is always faster overall
questions.explain: Gradient descent uses only first-order information and converges linearly with cheap steps; Newton's method uses the Hessian for quadratic convergence but each step requires forming and solving with that Hessian.
